speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: MAS supervises and works closely with financial institutions (FIs) to strengthen Singapore's defences against money laundering (ML), terrorism financing (TF) and financing of the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: I shall refer to these as "financial crimes" for convenience, throughout my speech.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: While FIs have made significant strides to strengthen their defences against financial crimes, they are currently unable to warn one another about unusual activity involving their customers, given customer confidentiality obligations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: Criminals exploit this by making illicit transactions through different FIs to avoid detection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: COSMIC will make it easier for FIs to detect and, thereby, deter criminal activity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: It will set out when and how such sharing of risk information relating to the customer may take place.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: The Bill also sets out robust legal and operational safeguards to protect the confidentiality of the information being shared and the interests of legitimate customers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: The Bill incorporates feedback from MAS' public consultation on COSMIC in October 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: The consultation received broad support for COSMIC and its objective of combatting financial crime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: As mentioned earlier, COSMIC will allow participant FIs to share with one another information, on a confidential basis, on customers whose profile or behaviour exhibits potential financial crime concerns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: Such risk information could include "red flag" behaviours and details of the concerning transaction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: Sharing on COSMIC would provide a recipient FI with better information to augment its risk understanding of a customer, thus enabling the FI to detect suspicious behaviour more accurately and expediently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: An FI may use this information to confirm if a customer's explanation for a financial transaction makes sense.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: If the FI assesses that the customer may be handling proceeds of a crime, it is required under existing law, specifically the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act 1992, to file a suspicious transaction report (STR) with the Singapore Police Force's Suspicious Transactions Reporting Office (STRO).

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: COSMIC will initially focus on three key risks which MAS and the Commercial Affairs Department (CAD) have identified, based on their observed cases relating to criminal networks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: These are areas which we have judged to benefit most from information sharing between FIs at scale, and which are also high on Singapore's priority list of risks, as identified through our continued risk surveillance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: The first risk area is the misuse of legal persons, for example, the abuse of shell companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: The ease of setting up a company and opening a corporate bank account supports the development of local enterprises and makes Singapore an attractive commercial centre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: But we do not want criminals to take advantage of this convenience to commit financial crime, by using legal persons such as shell companies to launder monies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: The misuse of legal persons to launder illicit proceeds and layer funds is also a concern related to international financial crime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: The second risk area is trade-based money laundering.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: This is the use of financing related to trade for illicit purposes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: As Singapore is a global commercial and trading hub, many companies here actively participate in and facilitate regional and global trade.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: Our FIs provide key services that enable such activity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: However, criminals can use trade as a disguise to transfer their illicit monies across borders undetected, for example, using fraudulent trade documents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: Suppliers and customers featured in a trade payment could be controlled by the same nefarious company that is trying to launder illicit funds under the guise of genuine businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: Mitigating trade-based money laundering is important to protect the trust in our FIs and companies, and to also protect legitimate trade flows.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: The third and last risk area is proliferation financing and the evasion of international sanctions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: Singapore's deep financial and trade linkages expose our FIs and companies to this risk.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: As a responsible member of the global community, Singapore must act strongly against the financing of such activity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: As information sharing under COSMIC is a new paradigm in the fight against financial crime, MAS plans to introduce COSMIC in phases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: MAS will prescribe the FIs that will participate in COSMIC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: They are DBS, OCBC, UOB, SCB, Citibank and HSBC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: This sharing of information between MAS and these six banks will be voluntary in this first phase.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: This allows the COSMIC platform to achieve operational stability, and also enables MAS to closely engage participant FIs to calibrate COSMIC's features and address operational concerns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: Subsequently, MAS plans to expand COSMIC's coverage to more focus areas and FIs, and make sharing mandatory in higher-risk circumstances.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: I will first elaborate on the scope of information sharing permitted on COSMIC, including the three modes and the objective thresholds for sharing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: I will also share about the safeguards in place to protect legitimate customers from being adversely impacted by such sharing, and also how data shared on COSMIC will be protected.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: I earlier mentioned that participant FIs may use COSMIC to share customer information with one another only for detecting or preventing financial crimes, if these customers exhibit multiple "red flags" that indicate potential financial crime concerns and if the stipulated thresholds are met.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: They relate to: one, a participant FI requesting information from another participant; two, a participant FI proactively providing information to another; and three, a participant FI placing the customer on a watchlist to alert other participant FIs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: An objective threshold needs to be crossed before information can be shared using any of the three modes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: Which mode is to be used is largely guided by the extent of a customer's "red flag" behaviours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: The "red flags" will correspond to known criminal profiles and behaviours for key financial crime risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: For example, where transaction activities are inconsistent with the business profile of the company and cannot be explained, or if there are clear discrepancies in supporting documents that also cannot be explained.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: Further, only multiple "red flags" may trigger information sharing on COSMIC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: This sets an objective and reasonably high threshold to ensure that COSMIC is used only for cases of significant concern and safeguards against frivolous requests that could unnecessarily expose customer risk information.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: However, the thresholds, details and permutations of the "red flags" must be kept strictly confidential among only the participant FIs, to prevent criminals from circumventing them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: For most customers, no "red flag" indicators will be triggered.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: For these customers, I wish to reiterate that participant FIs will not be permitted to share customer's information.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: In fact, COSMIC is intended to help identify and weed out nefarious companies more effectively, so that legitimate customers can operate in a trusted environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: Lastly, to ensure that we do not unduly impede legitimate sharing aimed at safeguarding our financial system, the Bill will also afford protection to participant FIs from civil suits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: This will provide participant FIs with confidence that legitimate information sharing to highlight higher risk customers and their related activities will not unduly expose them to legal challenge, which may even be brought by the very actors that COSMIC seeks to guard against.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: Notwithstanding, I would like to address possible situations where legitimate customers are inadvertently associated with bad actors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: For example, a company could end up unknowingly trading with an illicit counterparty and hence, be subject to a participant FI's scrutiny.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: There are safeguards in place to protect legitimate customers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: Participant FIs should first assess if there are valid reasons for the customer's behaviour or profile, before sharing information on COSMIC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: As part of the bank's risk assessment, banks are also expected to reach out to customers to allow them, to give them the opportunity to address the bank's risk concerns and to explain unusual behaviours observed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: Bank customers are thus strongly encouraged to be forthcoming and respond promptly to their bank's due diligence queries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: This will ensure that customers have a chance to explain and that legitimate customers are not inadvertently adversely impacted by sharing on COSMIC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: In addition, even after information has been shared on COSMIC, FIs must make an independent risk assessment of a customer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: An FI should not rely solely on the information received from COSMIC to terminate a customer relationship, including the fact that a customer has been placed on the "watchlist".

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: More broadly, MAS will require participant FIs to ensure accuracy and completeness of the information shared on COSMIC and to correct any errors or omissions, especially if a customer has provided further clarifications to address earlier financial crime concerns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: MAS will closely monitor how participant FIs use COSMIC information in cases where they had exited customer relationships, to ensure that customers are given opportunities to address the concerns of FIs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: As the owner of the COSMIC platform, MAS will ensure that COSMIC information is exchanged and stored securely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: The platform will have robust controls, including cybersecurity measures, such as data encryption and firewalls to block unauthorised external access.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: It will also have strict user access limitations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: These controls will be subject to periodic audits to ensure their efficacy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: This includes requirements to have systems and processes in place to prevent unauthorised use or disclosure of information obtained from COSMIC, and robust cybersecurity and encryption measures to safeguard information obtained from COSMIC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: MAS will be able to inspect participants' adherence to these measures and will not hesitate to take firm action if they uncover any breach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: This is necessary for MAS to monitor if participant FIs are using COSMIC appropriately, and will also support MAS' broader supervisory and surveillance role to ensure that FIs have robust defences against financial crime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: In parallel, adequate safeguards will be put in place to protect confidentiality of the information shared.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies)
text: This will strengthen Singapore's role and reputation as a safe, trusted and innovative global financial centre.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: While our defences against ML/TF/PF have strengthened over the years, MAS must continue in its commitment to refresh traditional policies, as we cannot combat new criminal typologies with old methods.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: A notable way in which ML/TF/PF crimes are perpetrated is by creating a web of individual accounts or through accounts of shell companies opened across different FIs to facilitate illicit fund flows.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: That said, I would like to seek some clarifications on this Bill and will start with COSMIC's coverage and implementation.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: While we welcome the inclusion of six major banks as a start, can the Minister clarify the expected effectiveness of COSMIC?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: For example, assuming COSMIC had been rolled out in the past year, how many more material cases of ML/TF/PF would be detected in this back test?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: I ask, as this would enable a clearer understanding of COSMIC's effectiveness with the six banks participating at onset, and to calibrate how fast it should scale to achieve a meaningful impact.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Relevant to this, I understand that the initial phase is planned to be approximately two years starting from second half of 2024, during which information is shared by the six banks only on a voluntary basis as the Minister had mentioned.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Considering that innovations in financial crime are rapidly evolving, it is crucial for COSMIC's implementation to be swift and effective.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: To this end, can the Minister explain how MAS will review and shorten this period, including mandating information sharing earlier if the platform proves to be stable and effective?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Digital financial services are also developing very, very quickly and as compared with traditional banks, regulations in this space are still maturing, which could encourage their usage as vectors for crime.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Against this backdrop, can the Minister elaborate on the plans for COSMIC to include fintech, payments and other virtual asset service providers?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Clause 28G of the Bill states that MAS will be issuing threshold criteria and high-risk indicators to participating FIs, which when met, mandates FIs to request, provide and publish risk information on COSMIC, under clauses 28D to F respectively.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: The criteria are confidential to avoid circumvention by bad actors.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Understandably, risk processes vary across sub-sectors and the different FIs have different risk appetites, some of which may be more conservative than COSMIC's.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: As COSMIC scales, can the Minister explain if FIs are able to leverage on COSMIC's information to meet their tighter risk standards than the required baseline, as stipulated in COSMIC's implementation?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Also, as we discuss this Bill, the exponential increase in scam cases comes to mind as was discussed in the earlier Bill, just a while ago.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Typically, scam proceeds are swiftly dissipated across different local and foreign bank accounts as part of a broad and organised money laundering network, which makes it challenging for authorities to trace and recover assets.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: With financial intelligence on companies, individuals and their related parties shared on a larger database used by multiple FIs and authorities, I am glad that the Bill has factored safeguards to ensure cybersecurity and data confidentiality.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Regarding cybersecurity, COSMIC is required to comply with the Government's security standards and have features like user authentication and data encryption.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: FIs must also implement controls to complement MAS' efforts in preventing information security breaches.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: As participating members, the effectiveness of each FI's controls will be crucial to uphold the security of the entire network.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: To this end, can the Minister share if there will be periodic reviews or audits conducted by MAS on the robustness of FI controls relevant to COSMIC?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Regarding data confidentiality, MAS has clarified that within the Government, only authorised officers from MAS and the Suspicious Transactions Reporting Office in the CAD will be able to directly access and use information from COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Clause 28K of the Bill sets out conditions for onward disclosure of information and Clause 28I accords statutory protection for FIs against civil liabilities.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Further to the provisions, can the Minister clarify if MAS or CAD may use information in COSMIC to assess, and/or subsequently, penalise a participating FI for any ML/TF/PF control lapse?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: It is only through the sharing of experiences by everyone that a clearer picture is formed.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: COSMIC can indeed help us piece together the clearer picture of financial crimes.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Over the years, MAS has closely supervised and worked with FIs to strengthen Singapore's defences to prevent ML/TF/PF.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: However, a weakness in the effective detection of illicit financial flows lies in the inability of FIs to alert one another to unusual activity in their customers' accounts.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Financial criminals exploit these "information silos" by making illicit transactions through a web of accounts in different FIs and moving from one FI to another to avoid detection.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This platform will enable FIs to conduct sharper analysis of customer behaviours and activities to detect potential illicit activities more promptly and warn each other of such activities.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: While starting with these banks with the largest local network might make sense, they are also the banks with the least to lose in turning down customers and are likely to have the most resources to pursue and file STRs or perform deep dives into customer networks and relationships.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: These banks are also the ones which would, in my opinion, likely face the most pushback from customers and special purpose vehicles set up to obfuscate identities when it comes to asking Know Your Client (KYC) questions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Adding a select group of such smaller offshore private banks into the start-up group of FIs for COSMIC would be advisable.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I encourage the Government to consider doing this as soon as practicable.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: While details will eventually be forthcoming, one concern – and I move on to my second point – is how prescriptive the subsidiary legislation from MAS will be.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Clear and prescriptive regulations would minimise confusion amongst participant banks over what specifically might constitute grounds for submission of information to COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The revised section 28E of the Bill makes clear under what conditions a FI may make disclosures to another FI in respect of a suspicious transaction, but does not seem to be as clearly prescriptive as to under what circumstances an FI is obligated, or expected, or required to report such information to another FI.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Would there be any change in this regard?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The actual framework of predetermined "red flags" will need to be comprehensive yet flexible enough.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Presumably this will be fleshed out in subsidiary regulations.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Otherwise, MAS and/or the STRO could become inundated with questions over whether such and such a transaction should be submitted to COSMIC, to which the reply might be that banks should conduct their own assessment and submit the information if deemed appropriate.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In other words, Mdm Deputy Speaker, sufficiently clear and prescriptive guidelines on what constitutes a transaction that should be submitted to another FI via COSMIC would be critical to prevent confusion and the possible over-submission of information.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Hence, I would urge MAS to issue these guidelines expeditiously and review these regularly in consultation with the FI community.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In relation to this particular point, the MAS, in its response to the consultation with FIs, said: "Information sharing on COSMIC will be done via a structured data template that will be made available to all participant FIs.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This will include fields for information relating to the customer including identifying information of the customer and the beneficial owners and authorised signatories of the customer, details of the transactions in question, the "red flag" behaviour exhibited and the risk analysis that is relevant to the customer relationship." I trust these templates, going forward in subsequent iterations, will be sufficiently granular to address the point that I have made.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Moving on to my third point, Mdm Deputy Speaker, the primary intent of this Bill is to enable information sharing between FIs on suspicious activity.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: However, paragraph 13.4 under MAS Notice 626 already gives FIs the power to share customer information with third parties without obtaining customer consent, if it is in relation to AML/CFT issues.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This paragraph reads: "13.4 For the purposes of complying with this Notice, a bank may, whether directly or through a third party, collect, use and disclose personal data of an individual customer, an individual beneficiary of a life insurance policy, an individual appointed to act on behalf of a customer, an individual connected party of a customer or an individual beneficial owner of a customer, without the respective individual's consent." Thus, it would be helpful if the Government could clarify just how this provision in MAS Notice 626 would interact with the provisions of this new Bill and COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: For example, can FIs share information about suspicious transactions or clients bilaterally, as it were, without reference to the COSMIC platform but taking reference instead from this provision in MAS Notice 626?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Or should all such information sharing henceforth be channelled through COSMIC and be transacted under the provisions of this Bill?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And secondly, how will these thresholds be benchmarked against global standards for illegal financial flows?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Next, Mdm Deputy Speaker, COSMIC is, at its heart, an online system where the key players are interacting in cyberspace.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: However, highly confidential financial information is being shared on this system.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Thus, a key concern is how COSMIC will be secured.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Would it be a special team at MAS or would this be outsourced to another Government agency or private company, and if so, which one?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The new system, thus created, will need to rest on clear regulatory guidelines, be frequently reviewed amidst a dynamic global financial services and financial crime environment, as well as powerful cybersecurity defences.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: With the growing sophistication of criminals engaged in financial crime who take advantage of information asymmetry between FIs, enforcement agencies and regulators within a global ecosystem, there is a case to require enhanced cooperation between FIs, even if they may be business competitors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In return, the FIs are immunised against civil liability for sharing information amongst them.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The basic idea is that, with the pooling of information between FIs, there is a better chance to know the nature of the beast that the FIs are dealing with.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I do not think there is any quarrel with the basic premise of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Like the hon Member Mr Derrick Goh who spoke before me, this too brings to my mind the famous Indian folktale of the six blind men and the elephant.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This story must have made an impact in our childhood.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Each of them touched a different part of the animal and came with a completely different assessment of how the elephant looked like.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: They later learnt though, that when they put together all the information that they have separately gleaned, only then did they know the truth of the matter.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The points I will be raising in my speech are focused on trying to better understand the mechanics of the proposed framework and how they can be reconciled against the stated aim of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Everyone wants to know the final shape of the beast, but what incentives are there for people who own each individual part to take the time and trouble to give up his piece and see where and how it fits?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In the event the discloser declines to disclose the risk information, it must notify the requester of its decision and the reasons for the same.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: There is no specific timeline specified for the discloser to reply to the requester through COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This is understandable as the time needed may be case specific.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: On the other hand, there should be a general understanding between FIs that requests for information should be dealt with urgency, so that there is a chance to catch up with the suspected criminals.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In the banking world, with transactions being completed in a matter of microseconds, speed of response is of utmost important.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Can we ask, for example, for guidelines – what is a reasonable time to respond?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I would also like to understand whether the framework will allow for redress against FIs, which are objectively assessed to be too conservative or even obstructive, in rejecting requests for risk information.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Such attitudes will undermine the aim of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: How do we assess when a specific FI is being unduly dismissive of a request which should have been taken more seriously?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In this regard, I note that it is proposed that MAS be given the power to issue notices, of a general or specific nature, to FIs for the effective administration of the information sharing framework.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Is it contemplated that this issue I raised will be dealt with through enforcement action permitted under the MAS notices?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: There is, in addition, a connected issue of parity on the part of FIs.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: They invest substantial amounts of money in compliance systems that will allow the banks to monitor real-time transactions and analyse them against a treasure trove of databases to flag suspicious activities.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: They also make significant investments into the training of compliance officers to act as competent gatekeepers for the respective banks.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I see this as a potential double-edged sword.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: On one hand, I would imagine that, at least theoretically, the bigger the number of FIs which can join COSMIC, the better protection we get from ML/TF/PF activities.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: On the other hand, by prescribing entry requirements, there is a possibility that the smaller FIs may be less motivated to make investments to qualify.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This will eliminate the moral hazard I am concerned about, but I am not sure if this is practicable.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The middle ground option would be to employ the 80-20 rule and just focus on banks of a certain size and above.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: However, this will be a dog whistle for the criminals to use smaller banks.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I would be grateful for the hon Minister of State's views on this matter.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The next operational issue I wish to touch on is the proposed ability on the part of a prescribed FI to, on its own motion, disclose risk information to another prescribed FI in certain circumstances as provided for under section 28E in the Bill.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: It makes the information-sharing platform much more effective.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: That is, what do you do if you suspect someone else has a piece?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: To depend on only the requesting FIs to initiate the information-sharing process assumes that the requestors will be able to identify "red flags".

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In all likelihood, there will continue to be blind spots in form of Donald Rumsfeld's "unknown unknowns" or going back to the parable of the blind men and the elephant.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Allowing FIs possessing the risk information to proactively share it with the relevant FIs, even without initiation by the latter, addresses this problem.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I note that the operative word here is "may".

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The question I have is what structural incentives or disincentives can be provided to the FIs so that they can be motivated to be proactive.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Would this be dealt with under the proposed MAS Notice?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I now turn to the area of enforcement against FIs to ensure compliance with the information-sharing framework.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I have two specific questions in this area.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I support the need to create this offence.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: There are serious repercussions for the customer if the FI gets it wrong.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The hon Minister of State acknowledged this in his speech.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The customer will be denied access to their bank accounts and probably would be subject of STRs that may trigger investigations by enforcement authorities.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This is the same for other statutes that MAS enforces, such as the Banking Act 1970 (BA) or the Financial Advisers Act.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: It is consistently provided that a person who negligently provided false information to the MAS is guilty of an offence.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: These provisions were enacted with the current paradigm of information flow in mind, that is, as between the FI and MAS.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In fact, I note that under the proposed section 28L in the Bill, MAS is not only entitled to a copy of the risk information that was shared by an FI to another FI, but can also act on it.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: If that is the case, why is it proposed that the consequence for negligently providing false information to MAS be dealt with differently from negligently providing false information to another FI?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I would be grateful for the hon Minister of State's clarification on this.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Under the proposed provisions, it seems that anyone may falsely describe to another the piece he has without consequence if it is attributable to lack of diligence on his part.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The entering into DPAs in lieu of prosecution provides the Public Prosecutor with an important tool to deal with corporate offending without affecting innocent stakeholders such as shareholders.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Typically, DPAs provide for detailed remediation on the part of the corporate offender, so as to ensure that proper systems are in place to prevent re-offending.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This may, in certain situations, serve public interest better.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Currently, the Sixth Schedule consists of a good number of offences in the AML/CFT arena, particularly the offences under the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act 1992 and section 16(4) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2022.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: But the difficulty is that the private entities have always had little incentive to produce public good.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The current Bill offers some ways for us to harness FIs to this end, and I hope my proposals will not just help us gather more pieces of the puzzle, but ensure that they fit in the right places as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: This makes it harder for criminals to use transfers across multiple FIs to avoid detection.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Despite the difficult economic climate, I am glad that Singapore remains an attractive financial centre, with increased fund inflows from an increase in the number of family offices from 400 in 2020, to over 700.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: As our transactions and assets increase, our ability to supervise these transactions must also improve.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I support this Bill as this will let us take the lead in detecting and preventing financial crime, strengthening Singapore's position as a major financial hub.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: My first point is on using COSMIC to tackle illegal wildlife trade.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: In my speech on the Endangered Species (Import and Export) (Amendment) Bill, I highlighted how there is evidence suggesting that Singapore is a critical nexus in the illegal wildlife trade.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: In the past decade, we have seized illegal shipments of animal parts worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Elephants, rhinoceroses, pangolins – these are just a few animals whose dead, dissected bodies are smuggled through Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Just a week later, we seized another 12.7 tonnes of pangolin scales.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: In October 2020, the National Parks Board (NParks) seized 34 kilogrammes of rhinoceros horns from a man travelling from South Africa to Laos through Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: This is the largest seizure of rhinoceros horns to-date.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Such seizures are just the tip of the iceberg.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Smugglers have found ways to circumvent our border security and bring these animals and their body parts onto our soil.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: When you look at the size and value of animal part seizures at our borders, we are talking about operations that must, by logic, involve financing, coordinating and operations on a large, organised scale.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: A $50 million shipment of pangolin scales is not the work of isolated individuals.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: These criminals have the know-how to avoid and evade detection through complicated transactions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: This is why we need a platform like this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Will MAS also work with investigators of wildlife crime to ensure COSMIC data is used to both identify perpetrators as well as help banks do so?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: By making this data available for stakeholders tackling wildlife crime, our financial sector will be able to play an important part in battling this illegal wildlife trade.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) has flagged the illegal wildlife trade as a major transnational organised crime.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It is a perfect candidate for the powers under this Bill and I hope MAS will take this into consideration as we develop this platform further.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: My second point is about the policing of privacy regulations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: This legislation does a good job balancing the goal of reducing economic crime with the concern of privacy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Banks obtaining information via COSMIC will only be able to share it in certain circumstances with a limited set of people, even within their own organisation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Cybersecurity measures must also be in place to protect the information.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But how will MAS ensure that banks hold themselves up to these standards?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: If a bank officer forwards it to a colleague who should not have access to the information, how will MAS find out?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Will there be data audits to track the flow of COSMIC information within and out of banks?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Information obtained from COSMIC will be highly sensitive and improper circulation may have serious implications for those targeted.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: MAS must ensure banks protect the information properly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: My third and final point is on how COSMIC data will be processed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Having aggregated data from multiple FIs like this is a valuable resource with great potential.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: MAS has stated that the STRO will have access to data from COSMIC for its analysis.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the Minister clarify whether there are further plans to provide other Government agencies or FIs access to the COSMIC data?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: On one hand, this data could be mined to gain valuable insights about suspicious activity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: This could even be shared internationally to strengthen enforcement globally.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: On the other hand, the processing of such data must be carefully governed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It must not be done in a way that might breach confidentiality.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It should not be analysed by banks for commercial business purposes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Since this relates to allegations of criminal conduct, machine learning or artificial intelligence models analysing the data must also be carefully managed to avoid any bias.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: If there are plans to share COSMIC data with other entities, can the Minister share what safeguards are in place?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I support the Bill, but I have few points to clarify with the Minister.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What are the job roles within these six banks which are authorised to access such information?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Assuming the bank's compliance officer is authorised to retrieve the information shared by another bank, is there a Chinese wall that prevents the information from being shared with the salespeople?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How does MAS prevent these banks from abusing the information obtained from their competitors?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: All banks are required to participate in the Credit Bureau, which is the central repository of credit information for individuals and businesses in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It collects and maintains credit-related data, such as credit accounts, repayment records and bankruptcy information from all banks that are licensed by MAS.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This centralised system allows lenders to access a borrower's credit history from a single source rather than having to collect the information themselves.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This helps to reduce the risk of lending and makes the lending process more efficient.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Will people with ill-intent not bank with the other FIs which do not subscribe to COSMIC so as to circumvent detection?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How are the thresholds being determined and what are the "red flags" and transactions that will be flagged?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How does MAS intend to synergise the information that it collects via COSMIC with the STR that these six banks file with the STRO so as to strengthen the risk monitoring of the financial sector?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Will the enhanced intelligence be shared with other Government agencies, such as the Singapore Police Force and the Attorney-General's Chambers, to investigate and prosecute money laundering and terrorism financing cases?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Do the participating banks need to pay a subscription fee or transaction fee?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Singapore's position as a finance and business hub is strengthened after COVID-19 and we are seeing a record number of family offices and high net-worth individuals transferring their assets to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is important for MAS to share about the risks and implications of money laundering and terrorism financing with their bankers and fund managers.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This could include the development of tailored training programmes and seminars, as well as the dissemination of information and guidance materials to promote greater awareness and understanding of these issues, which may implicate Singapore's reputation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It seeks to safeguard Singapore's status as a key financial centre and node for transactions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The finance industry today is turbocharged by technology.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This facilitates business and trade, but at the same time, it gives rise to vulnerabilities for easy funding of illicit activities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must be careful not to sully our hub status by allowing cases of ML/TF/PF to take place.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Considering that it is voluntary to participate, what would incentivise banks to do so?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: After all, client confidentiality is paramount for most banks, especially larger ones that rely on customer loyalty.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Many would be concerned with information sharing with affiliates of the participating banks outside Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Moreover, it is worth noting that certain banks are alleged to have been involved in scandals related to the very transgressions this Bill seeks to remedy.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As such, why would they choose to come forward on their own accord and potentially put their business at risk?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Also, given that banks will still have to conduct the usual KYC checks and continue to report suspicious transactions, this new platform, in some way, may overlap with what is already in the market.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As such, how will this Bill enhance these efforts?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Banks using COSMIC may also question the source of the information.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For example, there may be queries on what information did the reporting banks base their report on?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What is or is not good information can also be quite subjective.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some banks may take the view that they should report everything even remotely suspicious.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: There may also be unintended consequences of using COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For instance, clients, potential clients or third parties may even be able to work out which of the banks have stricter or more relaxed ML/TF/PF policies since everyone will eventually be working off the same set of information on COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, what happens after the discovery of irregularities?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If banks share information about transactions suspected of being involved in ML/TF/PF activities, will the transactions be further investigated?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: There may also be liability issues in instances where one bank acted wrongly or inaccurately, based on information provided by another bank.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Would MAS or another agency be double checking the veracity of the information?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Although banks are protected against civil suits, does the Bill grant them immunity from clients for the breach of confidentiality, particularly if the suspicion of illicit transactions is later proven to be unfounded?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Likewise, are banks immune from litigation by MAS if their transactions are investigated?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Third, the fact alone that ML/TF/PF activities are often cross-border in nature poses a significant challenge to the feasibility of the framework.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As these activities tend to involve multiple banks or branches overseas, how does this Bill aid in this aspect, in getting overseas branches to share information?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Fourth, what are the triggers for information sharing?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What are the safeguards in place to ensure that information is not shared too easily?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is important that we have a comprehensive and consistent approach to combat financial crime across all FIs operating in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Members' comments and queries can be categorised into a few themes and I will address them in turn.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked how COSMIC will be used to address scams.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is why the Singapore Government has partnered the industry and is taking a multi-pronged approach to combat the threat of scams.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: COSMIC is not intended to duplicate or replicate the good work done by the Anti-Scam Command.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: That said, one of the key financial crime risks that COSMIC will initially focus on is the misuse of legal persons, such as shell companies, which I mentioned in my speech.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Scam syndicates may use shell companies to receive victims' money directly or as a conduit to layer and launder their criminal proceeds.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: COSMIC will enable FIs to share relevant financial crime concerns on such suspicious accounts and transactions relating to shell companies with one another, if the thresholds are met.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is so that the FIs can take the necessary mitigation measures and alert the authorities.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Louis Ng had asked if the scope of COSMIC will be expanded to other risk areas, including wildlife crime and I know we talked about elephants, rhinoceroses and pangolins.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: However, in the initial phase, COSMIC will focus on the three risk areas I mentioned, which have been identified for prioritisation through our continued risk surveillance.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Keeping this focus would also allow participant FIs adequate time to familiarise themselves with this new information-sharing paradigm.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Thereafter, MAS will consider expanding COSMIC's scope to other key risks.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked if COSMIC may be less effective at the start with only six banks as its initial participants.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Goh also asked about plans to include fintech and other digital payment firms on COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Leon Perera asked about the inclusion of smaller offshore and private banks in the initial phase of COSMIC, given their potential exposure to financial crime risks.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Murali Pillai noted that as COSMIC expands to include more FIs, FIs that have lower compliance capabilities and capacities may unfairly leverage off FIs which do.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Don Wee also asked if criminals may use FIs that are not on COSMIC to circumvent detection.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Please allow me to answer these questions together.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I mentioned that COSMIC will initially focus on the misuse of legal persons as well as trade-based ML and proliferation financing.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These risks manifest themselves in the commercial and small- and medium-sized enterprises banking space, of which the initial six participant banks have significant market share.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Fintech and digital payment firms are not currently operating at quite the same scale.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: However, as I mentioned in my speech, MAS will consider expanding the scope of COSMIC to more banks and other FIs in other or future phases.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Ahead of this, MAS will continue to work with the industry to improve their capabilities, including using data analytics, to enable their potential participation in COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will closely monitor the potential risk migration to FIs not yet on COSMIC – so, outside of these six banks – and will take preventive or supervisory measures as necessary.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will continue to work closely with participating FIs to track COSMIC's effectiveness and to make the needed adjustments on an ongoing basis.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I will move on to safeguards and confidentiality of COSMIC information which is of interest to Members.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Don Wee asked how sharing information on COSMIC will interact with the data protection requirements in the PDPA and banking confidentiality obligations in the BA.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Louis Ng, Mr Don Wee and Mr Leon Perera asked about the strict safeguards to protect information obtained from COSMIC, including those related to cybersecurity.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Derrick Goh also asked about the roles and responsibilities of the participating FIs and MAS, in the event of a cybersecurity incident on COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Bill seeks to strike a balance between protecting the privacy of legitimate customers and also preventing criminal abuse of this protection to conceal serious financial crime.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Bill will permit sharing of information between FIs for financial crime prevention and detection purposes within tightly circumscribed parameters.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Customer consent will not be required for sharing on COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Because criminals are unlikely to agree to allow their information to be shared.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Bill will also disapply sections 21 and 22 of PDPA, which relate to access and correction of personal data.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: FIs will, however, still be required to take measures to ensure the accuracy and completeness of the information shared on COSMIC under the Bill.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is different from the COSMIC initiative – he asked about the difference between Notice 626 and COSMIC – because COSMIC seeks to allow participant financial institutions to share customer information with one another.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The safeguards of and for information shared on COSMIC apply at two levels.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First, MAS is the owner and operator of the COSMIC platform and MAS will ensure that COSMIC information is exchanged and stored securely, with strict cybersecurity measures, which include data encryption.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I also mentioned that these controls will be subject to audits, both internal and external, to ensure their effectiveness.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Second, at the participant FI level, they are likewise required to adopt strong safeguards, such as allowing only a small group of the FIs' authorised officers to access COSMIC and also sharing COSMIC risk information only within the boundaries permitted by the Bill.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These MAS-regulated FIs are required to institute robust controls, including cybersecurity and data protection controls, to prevent information security breaches.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will closely supervise participants' adherence to these measures and will take firm action for any lapses, including breaches which result in customer information leakage.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In the event of a cybersecurity breach, MAS will work closely with the FIs to promptly remediate the issue and conduct a postmortem to assess the need on whether to tighten the defences further.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Next, on the effectiveness of voluntary sharing and how we can scale up the sharing.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Yip and Mr Murali Pillai asked about the incentive for banks to voluntarily participate in COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: COSMIC is built upon the foundation of the positive experience of sharing between CAD, MAS and banks under the AML/CFT Industry Partnership (ACIP), which the six participant FIs are members of.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Case-specific information sharing under ACIP, on a smaller scale than what is envisioned for COSMIC, has already fostered mutual trust.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The six participant FIs are keen to build on these early efforts to continue and expand the sharing through COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Yip and Mr Derrick Goh were concerned that banks may have varying levels of AML/CFT policies and risk appetite on when to share information on COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Yip also noted that there must also be safeguards in place to ensure that information is not too readily shared on COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Leon Perera suggested that there should be sufficiently prescriptive and granular guidelines on when FIs should share information on COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked if this initial voluntary phase could be shortened, given the rapid innovations in financial crime.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Murali Pillai also asked whether the COSMIC framework addresses FIs that are too conservative or obstructive in rejecting requests for information, and whether there are penalties for this.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Leon Perera also asked how frequently the "red flags" and thresholds would be reviewed.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If I could reference my speech earlier, I explained how MAS has worked with the initial six participating banks to develop clear and objective thresholds for sharing information on COSMIC, as well as expectations on engaging customers.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will continue to work closely with the participating FIs to ensure the "red flags" and threshold criteria remain effective in targeting financial crime behaviour and also to review them if necessary.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will monitor FIs' usage of COSMIC to ensure that they are consistent in their assessment of when information should be shared on COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked about the timelines for FIs to respond to or to provide information on COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These timelines are designed to enable FIs to share risk information on a timelier basis, so that they can take earlier mitigation measures.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The design of the timeline must also be balanced against the time needed for the FIs themselves to engage customers to clarify the "red flags" and concerns, so that the legitimate customers will not have their information unnecessarily shared on COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, you need that time to allow for us to make sure that that is so.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I will move on to the STR filing and the accuracy of COSMIC information.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Yip asked about potential overlaps between FIs' obligation to report suspicious transactions and to also share information on COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Don Wee asked if COSMIC can be built upon existing systems, such as STRO's platform.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: He also asked if MAS is funding the development of COSMIC and whether participating FIs need to pay any fee.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Sharing of information on COSMIC is meant to strengthen the FIs' ability to collectively detect potential bad actors when stipulated "red flag" thresholds are crossed.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Information sharing under the Request or Provide modes will take place even before the threshold for filing an STR is crossed.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This will allow more holistic understanding of customers exhibiting sufficient "red flags", and more timely management by the FIs.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If the FIs subsequently file an STR, the deeper insights gleaned from COSMIC and included in the STR would be more helpful for law enforcement.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As STRO's platform is used by a much wider pool of both FIs and non-FIs to report suspicions relating to financial crime activity that have been established on reasonable grounds, it would not be appropriate to integrate the STRO platform with COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: However, and nonetheless, MAS is exploring if the STR and COSMIC processes could be streamlined to reduce the administrative burden on participant FIs.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, I thank the Member for that feedback.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: However, they are expected to ensure sufficient resourcing to support their effective participation on COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This includes maintaining and effecting any necessary upgrade of data analytical tools, as COSMIC's information sharing is integrated into their internal platforms.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I will move on to the accuracy of COSMIC information.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about FIs relying on information from COSMIC and how to ensure the accuracy as well as the reliability of risk concerns that are shared by other FIs.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: He also asked about FIs' liability from sharing or using information on COSMIC should it turn out to be inaccurate.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Murali Pillai also asked why it has not been proposed for FIs which are negligent in making false or misleading disclosures to be guilty of an offence.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Derrick Goh also asked how FIs would use information from COSMIC, given their varying risk management standards.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As I mentioned, participant FIs will be required to ensure accuracy and completeness of the information shared on COSMIC and to correct any errors or omissions, for example, in instances where a customer has provided further clarifications.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This same standard is also found in various provisions of other statutes which MAS administers, such as the BA, which relate to the provision of information that is false or misleading.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We adopted this standard of care, given the need to balance between ensuring accuracy of information and also not inadvertently deterring participants from sharing information.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: COSMIC is meant to provide an additional information source to supplement our FIs' existing sources and to also enhance their risk assessments of their own customers, in line with their internal risk management standards.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As such, MAS expects FIs to also carry out their own due diligence, including conducting further public source checks as well as seeking clarifications with their customers in such risk assessments.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As part of MAS' supervision, MAS will consider circumstances of relevant breaches arising from the use of COSMIC information in assessing if there are any appropriate action to be taken.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Murali Pillai also suggested that the proposed offences committed by FIs under COSMIC be considered for listing under the Sixth Schedule of the CPC, which sets out offences in respect of which deferred prosecution agreements may be entered into.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We thank Mr Murali Pillai for this suggestion and will keep it in mind for when we roll out future phases of COSMIC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Yip Hong Weng asked if participant FIs are required to analyse information they receive from COSMIC and take risk mitigation actions if needed.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Louis Ng asked if there are plans to share COSMIC information with other Government agencies besides STRO and, if so, which safeguards would be in place.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Nominated Member Ms Janet Ang had also noted the usefulness of COSMIC information in her speech yesterday on the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) (Amendment) Bill and the Computer Misuse (Amendment) Bill and had asked how COSMIC information might be helpful in the enforcement of both these Bills.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will include information from COSMIC, including material networks of suspicious actors detected by the COSMIC platform, in our risk analysis and surveillance to target higher risk activities in the financial system for supervisory intervention.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Currently, MAS is able to share information in its possession with domestic authorities, including CAD, to facilitate their investigation, enforcement or supervisory action.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This may include information obtained through COSMIC where there is a financial crime concern.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Such sharing will be subject to conditions, including confidentiality safeguards.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Yip also asked about the sharing of COSMIC information with overseas branches, given that ML/TF/PF activities are often cross-border in nature.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: At present, FIs in Singapore can already disclose customer information for risk management purposes within the financial group, including with its overseas branches or subsidiaries.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This strengthens group-wide ML/TF/PF risk mitigation, and it prevents bad actors from moving between FIs within the same group and it is aligned with international standards set by the FATF.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With this, Madam, I beg to move.      .
